messages.content: Could you retrieve the 10-day weather forecast for the campsite at 35.68 latitude and -121.34 longitude, including daily temperature in Fahrenheit and total precipitation in inches?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

That returns office and grid coordinates. Then fetch forecast. But we can also use the forecast endpoint with lat/lon: https://api.weather.gov/points/{lat},{lon}/forecast?format=json. That returns forecast periods. We need 10-day forecast. The forecast endpoint returns 7-day forecast by default. There's also /forecast/daily for daily forecast. That returns daily periods. The forecast/daily returns periods with temperature, temperatureUnit, temperatureMax, temperatureMin, etc. For precipitation, it may include precipitation probability, precipitation amount? The daily forecast includes precipitation probability and precipitation amount? Let's check typical NWS daily forecast JSON. It includes "periods": array of objects with "temperature", "temperatureUnit", "temperatureMax", "temperatureMin", "shortForecast", "detailedForecast", "windSpeed", "windDirection", "icon", "startTime", "endTime", "isDaytime", "probabilityOfPrecipitation", "precipitation". The "precipitation" field may have "value" and "unitCode". The unitCode might be "unit:in" for inches. So we can parse that.

Thus we need to call the function with URL: "https://api.weather.gov/points/35.68,-121.34/forecast/daily?format=json". Provide headers Accept: application/json. Use default timeout. Then parse the JSON. Then extract first 10 periods. For each period, get temperature (likely "temperature" field). Temperature unit is Fahrenheit. Precipitation: if "precipitation" exists, get "value" and unitCode. If unitCode is "unit:in", then it's inches. If missing, maybe 0. Also "probabilityOfPrecipitation" may exist. But we need total precipitation in inches. So we can use "precipitation.value" if present. If not, maybe 0. Or we can use "probabilityOfPrecipitation" to estimate? But the requirement says "total precipitation in inches". So we use precipitation.value.
